test_cases.question: What proof do we need to keep when we process data based on user consent?
test_cases.answer: The controller must be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to the processing of his or her personal data. This means maintaining records or evidence that show consent was obtained.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of his or her personal data.

test_cases.question: If a user gives consent as part of a terms of service document, what requirements must that consent meet?
test_cases.answer: The request for consent must be presented in a clearly distinguishable manner from the other matters in the document, using an intelligible and easily accessible form with clear and plain language. Any part of the declaration that constitutes an infringement of the Regulation is not binding on the user.
test_cases.supporting_quote: If the data subject's consent is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters, the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language

test_cases.question: Can a data subject withdraw their consent after they have already given it?
test_cases.answer: Yes. The data subject shall have the right to withdraw their consent at any time. The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.
test_cases.supporting_quote: The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time

test_cases.question: If someone withdraws their consent to data processing, does that make any previous data collection illegal?
test_cases.answer: No. The withdrawal of consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing that was based on consent before the withdrawal. The data processed while consent was still valid remains lawfully processed.
test_cases.supporting_quote: The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal

test_cases.question: What must users be told about withdrawing consent, and how easy must the withdrawal process be?
test_cases.answer: Prior to giving consent, the data subject must be informed of their right to withdraw consent at any time. Additionally, it must be as easy to withdraw consent as it is to give it. Organizations cannot make the withdrawal process more burdensome than the original consent process.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Prior to giving consent, the data subject shall be informed thereof. It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent.
key_phrases: as easy to withdraw as to give

test_cases.question: Can a company require users to consent to non-essential data processing as a condition of signing up for a free service?
test_cases.answer: No. When assessing whether consent is freely given, the company must take utmost account of whether the performance of a contract—including the provision of a service—is conditional on consent to processing that is not necessary for performing that contract. If it is, the consent is likely not freely given.
test_cases.supporting_quote: When assessing whether consent is freely given, utmost account shall be taken of whether, inter alia, the performance of a contract, including the provision of a service, is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract

coverage.7(1): Test case 1 - Controller must demonstrate consent
coverage.7(2): Test case 2 - Written declaration requirements (distinguishable, clear, plain language)
coverage.7(3) right: Test case 3 - Right to withdraw at any time
coverage.7(3) prior lawfulness: Test case 4 - Withdrawal doesn't affect prior processing
coverage.7(3) informed + easy: Test case 5 - NEW - Must inform before, withdrawal as easy as giving
coverage.7(4): Test case 6 - Freely given assessment (contract conditional on unnecessary consent)

b2b_relevance: HIGH - Article 7 governs consent validity. Critical for: user registration flows, marketing consent, cookie consent, terms of service integration, and consent withdrawal mechanisms. The 'freely given' test (7(4)) is particularly important for freemium SaaS models—you cannot bundle unnecessary data processing consent with service access.
